description: Known, justified differences from the Python reference. Each rule names the scenarios and diff paths it covers ("*" is a wildcard), the languages it applies to, a predicate the actual value must satisfy, and the reason. Predicates: any, nonempty_string, naive_as_utc, tz_alias, jsondecode_equivalent, {"regex": "..."} (applied to the actual value).

predicate.regex: (?i)^(?!.*(unrecognized method|no method or field named|undefined function)).*\S

rules.reason: Python raises TypeError with its own wording (it names the Python function). R and MATLAB raise their native missing-argument error. That the call raises, and that no request is sent, is still compared. The predicate rejects messages saying the method itself does not exist.

For a 200 JSON body that is not an object the Python handler fails inside data.get() and returns str(AttributeError), e.g. "'list' object has no attribute 'get'". The text is a Python interpreter message; status and error_type (unknown_error) are still compared. The 'Error processing response:' prefix of the utilities module is rejected because in the combined api class the order module's handler wins the method resolution order and never adds it.

The text after the fixed 'HTTP error occurred: ' prefix is the HTTP library's own exception message (httpx in Python, libcurl in R, the MATLAB HTTP stack). The prefix, status and error_type are still compared.
The text after the fixed prefix is the host exception (Python prints KeyError('timestamp') as 'timestamp' in quotes). error_type and raw_data are still compared.

For D/W/M intervals pandas returns naive timestamps (the unix seconds read as UTC wall time, no zone). R has no naive date-time class, so POSIXct in UTC is the faithful equivalent: same instant and same wall-clock text, only the zone label differs.
MATLAB's time zone database reports Asia/Kolkata by its legacy IANA link name Asia/Calcutta. Both names denote the same zone; the ISO timestamps with their +05:30 offsets are still compared exactly.

The MATLAB client decodes responses with MATLAB's jsondecode, the platform convention. It has no null, so null becomes [] (tested with isempty), and a one-element array of objects becomes a 1x1 struct, which in MATLAB is the same value as a one-element struct array (numel is 1, r.data(1) works). The predicate accepts only these two collapses, recursively; every key, string, number and other array length must still match.

Python rejects a single dict as 'Positions must be an array'. In MATLAB a struct is a 1x1 struct array, and the documented positions argument accepts a struct array, so a single struct is a one-position list. The client sends a correct one-element positions array; the reported 404 only means this scenario defines no mock response, because Python sends nothing.
